original_question: Does every polynomial threshold function representation of the inner product mod 2 function IP_{2n} : F2^{2n} -> {-1,1} require at least 3^n monomials?
target_in_paper: The unnumbered open-problem entry "PTF Sparsity for Inner Product Mod 2" in arXiv:1204.6447. This paper is a compendium of open problems, so the prompt's reference to Conjecture 1.1 / Proposition 1.2 / Theorem 1.3 does not match this arXiv ID.
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper's official formulation. It targets the exact open problem about polynomial-threshold-function sparsity for the inner product mod 2 function on 2n bits, uses the correct function name IP_{2n}, and asks for the exact lower bound 3^n. It also stays on the basic question stated in the paper rather than drifting to the stronger XOR-product variant mentioned only in the remark.
missing_details: To be fully stand-alone, the question should define the function explicitly: for x,y in F_2^n, IP_{2n}(x,y) = (-1)^{sum_{i=1}^n x_i y_i}, where the sum is mod 2.

The paper uses the standard term "PTF representation" without re-defining it locally; a stand-alone version should say that this means a real polynomial p whose sign matches the function on the Boolean cube.

Because the input space is written as F_2^{2n} but the representing polynomial is real-valued, a self-contained statement should make explicit that the polynomial is evaluated on Boolean inputs identified with {0,1}^{2n}.
A fully explicit version should remove sign ambiguity by saying p(z) > 0 when IP_{2n}(z)=1 and p(z) < 0 when IP_{2n}(z)=-1 for every Boolean input z.
The coefficient field of the representing polynomial is implicit in the paper; it should be stated to be over the reals.
The statement is quantified over every positive integer n, not merely over infinitely many n or all sufficiently large n.
The monomial count should be stated as the number of nonzero monomials (nonzero-coefficient terms) in the representing polynomial.
No degree restriction is part of the paper's question; a paper-faithful stand-alone version should make clear that the lower bound is asked with no restriction on degree.
No homogeneity assumption appears in the paper.
No nilpotency or quotient-ring condition appears in the paper.

The nearby bullet about f xor g giving multiplicative lower bounds is described by the paper as a "much stronger statement," not as an equivalent reformulation, so it should not replace the main question.
refined_question: For every positive integer n, let IP_{2n}: F_2^{2n} -> {-1,1} be the inner-product-mod-2 function defined by IP_{2n}(x,y) = (-1)^{sum_{i=1}^n x_i y_i}, where x,y in F_2^n and the sum is taken modulo 2. Is it true that every real polynomial p(x_1,...,x_n,y_1,...,y_n), with no restriction on degree, such that p(x,y) > 0 exactly when IP_{2n}(x,y)=1 and p(x,y) < 0 exactly when IP_{2n}(x,y)=-1 for all (x,y) in {0,1}^{2n}, must contain at least 3^n nonzero monomials?
justification: The exact target is the page-9 entry titled "PTF Sparsity for Inner Product Mod 2," whose statement asks essentially your question verbatim. Unlike the paper described in your instructions, arXiv:1204.6447 is not organized around numbered conjectures and theorems; it is an open-problems list. The front matter explicitly says that notation and definitions are assumed from external standard Boolean-function references rather than developed in the note itself, so the only needed sharpening is to spell out the standard implicit pieces: the formula for IP_{2n}, what a PTF representation means, that the representing polynomial is real-valued, that monomial count means nonzero monomials, and that there is no extra degree/homogeneity restriction. The only nearby variant in the paper is a separate remark labeled "much stronger," so it is context rather than an equivalent restatement.
